name: GA-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a 15-point Republican partisan lean
Incumbent Austin Scott seeking re-election with a large financial advantage
Democratic challenger Kelly Esti has raised only about $19,000 with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price Republican win chances at roughly 98%
model.rationale: The district's 15-point Republican lean, Scott's incumbency, and his roughly 60-to-1 fundraising edge over Esti leave the Democrat with no visible path. Markets price this as a near-certain Republican hold, and no polling or expert ratings suggest otherwise.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected incumbent scandal would be the only plausible sources of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Austin Scott is seeking another term in a central Georgia district that leans heavily Republican, giving Democrats a 15-point deficit before any campaign factors are considered. Scott enters the general election with about $1.3 million on hand after raising over $1.1 million, while challenger Kelly Esti has raised under $20,000 and reports minimal cash. No outside groups are meaningfully engaged on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Republican win odds near 98 percent. With the incumbent well-funded in a friendly district and the challenger lacking resources, the seat is rated Safe Republican.
